title: Growth sync playbook - prep for Talia Brooks
body:
Purpose: prep notes for an 1:1 with Talia (IC, Senior Infra Engineer) — focus on growth conversation, quick status check on ongoing blockers, and alignment on Q4 priorities. Meeting length 30m. Tone: coaching + unblock. Want to leave with 2 concrete actions and clarity on time allocation for next sprint.

Context notes (quick headline for myself):
- Talia shipped the prefix-caching patch for replica selector last sprint; landed but saw a 6% regression in p99 on tail traces for short sequences (TODO: trace analysis).
- Expressed interest in more ownership of rollout and runbook automation (mentioned in last 1:1).
- Recently worked on pairing with Lina (SRE) on warm-up behavior; positive cross-team feedback.
- Career ask last time: opportunities to mentor/junior-eng ownership and a path to Staff-level impact.
- Current focus: reduce per-token cost with smarter batching while preserving latency SLO.

Pre-meeting checklist (things I should have ready):
- Quick dashboard snapshot: PR throughput last 14d, job queue length, p50/p95/p99 latency trends for short-seq vs long-seq. (I will pull the graphs from Console before the meeting.)
- Link to the failing traces, and the two test runs that reproduced the 6% p99 shift (JIRA-ENG-4127).
- Draft proposal for a micro-ownership charter (small set of infra features she could lead) — one pager.
- List of potential mentees (2) and a proposed shadow-oncall schedule.

Agenda (30m):
0-3m: quick personal check-in (how are you, energy, time off upcoming).
3-10m: technical status + blockers — hear Talia's view of the prefix-caching rollout and trace findings.
10-18m: growth / career — discuss concrete pathways to Staff-ish work: project types, leadership behaviors, mentoring.
18-26m: priorities & capacity — align on time allocation for next sprint (focus vs. maintain), discuss what to deprioritize.
26-30m: recap + action items (2–3 tangible next steps, owners, dates).

Suggested opening lines: "Quick personal check — how's the week going? I want to spend most of the time on the cache rollout + your growth plan. I have 30 minutes — is there anything urgent to surface?"

Questions to surface (coaching prompts):
- What did the traces teach you about the p99 shift? Where do you think the extra latency is originating (scheduling, batching times, kernel variance)?
- If you had 3 weeks of uninterrupted time, what would you build to make rollout observability + rollback safer?
- Which pieces of ownership do you want to own end-to-end vs. collaborate on? (e.g., rollout policy, runbook, test harness, dashboards)
- How do you prefer to level up others (direct mentoring, code reviews, pairing sessions)?

Running notes (things to jot down during the meeting):
- Talia's immediate hypothesis for p99 regression (write verbatim).
- Any experiments she wants to run (config flip, kernel variant test, longer trace sampling).
- Her appetite for taking lead on a small cross-functional feature (yes/no, timeline).
- Signals that would indicate success for a Staff-style project (measurable outcomes).

Proposed growth pathways (options to discuss):
A) Technical lead on rollout automation (ownership of rollout design, can lead 8-week project: rollout orchestration + automatic safe-fallbacks). Outcome: measurable reduction in manual rollback incidents; defined runbook; run oncall playbook.
B) Mentorship lead for new infra hires (pairing curriculum, weekly office hours, review rubric). Outcome: two engineers onboarded with paired PRs and dev-reviews.
C) Decomp into a cross-team reliability initiative (partner with SRE to tighten warm-up behavior and warm pool sizing). Outcome: 10% fewer cold-start tokens and improved stable tail latency.

Coach prompts for each option:
- A (rollout automation): what decision points will you need cross-team buy-in on? Who are the three stakeholders?
- B (mentorship): what time commitment feels sustainable (hours/week)? What would success look like at 3 months?
- C (reliability init): what data do you need to make the case (graphs, cost delta, incident examples)?

Prioritization & capacity (proposal to present):
- Next sprint: allocate 50% focus to rollout automation PoC (2-week spike) + 40% to maintenance/bugs + 10% slack/mentoring.
- Alternative: if on-call risk increases, flip to 60% maintenance for the sprint.

Concrete follow-ups to propose at end of meeting (I want these to be explicit):
1) Talia to run two controlled experiments (kernel variant + batching threshold) and share results by 2026-12-01. Owner: Talia. Deliverable: short write-up + dashboard link.
2) I (Marco) to draft a micro-ownership charter for rollout automation with proposed stakeholders and a 6–8 week timeline by 2026-11-30. Owner: Marco.
3) If she opts for mentorship track, identify mentee pair and set up first office hours by 2026-12-08. Owner: Talia.

Risk signals to watch (if raised, escalate to me / product):
- If experiment shows p99 regression persists after batching config changes and kernel variant, raise an incident review and pause rollout.
- If Talia reports bandwidth <25% due to incident/bugs, re-evaluate timeline and pull a secondary owner.

How I'll follow up after meeting (my cadence):
- Slack 1:1 summary (DM to Talia) within 24 hours with agreed actions + owners.
- Block a 30-min sync in two weeks to review experiment results and charter draft.

Notes for retro reference (what to record later in Confluence):
- Decision made about ownership path and the selected project.
- Outcomes of experiments and whether rollback was needed.
- Mentoring impact (if chosen): list mentee PRs and improvements.

Quick template for the Slack 1:1 summary (to paste and send):
"Thanks for today — notes: 1) Talia will run kernel + batching experiments, report by 2026-12-01; 2) I'll share a micro-ownership charter draft by 2026-11-30; 3) if you choose mentorship, set up office hours by 2026-12-08. I'll schedule a 30-min follow-up in two weeks. Anything I missed?"

Utility snippets and prompts I might paste into Jira / PR comments during conversation:
- "Assigning to @TaliaBrooks for experiment runs — please add the experiment config and dashboard link to JIRA-ENG-4127."
- "If we observe persistent p99 shift after config flips, pause rollout and notify #serving-runtime immediately."

Open questions I want answered in the meeting (so I can capture them as action items):
- Do you want the rollout automation project to be owned primarily by infra or be a joint infra+SRE charter?
- How much of your current sprint can be reallocated without creating churn in oncall?

Back-channel note to myself: be mindful to not over-prescribe. Offer options and help remove blockers (stakeholder introductions, small budget for observability probes, temporary headcount support).

End of doc.
